source: Leicestershire CC 2026/27 budget (ModernGov democracy.leics.gov.uk doc s194714, Cabinet 3 Feb / Council 18 Feb 2026, verified) + the AI DOGE directorate engine.

directorates.name: Children and Family Services
directorates._note: 4-year savings total; largest growth pressure (LAC placements + UASC).

cross_cutting._note: 4-year savings programme GBP 48.4m by directorate (GBP 23m in 2026/27), plus a separate GBP 66.1m DSG/High Needs programme; engine risk-adjusts the directorate programme to ~GBP 28.0m EV.

reserves._note: General Fund GBP 26m (4.2% of net budget) + earmarked GBP 171m incl Budget Equalisation GBP 113m; DSG reserve at minus GBP 96m; earmarked forecast overdrawn ~64m by Mar 2028 due to the DSG deficit.

risks.risk: DSG High Needs accumulated deficit GBP 64.4m (24/25) forecast GBP 111.9m (25/26), the cumulative DSG gap heading to ~GBP 265m by the statutory override end (31 March 2028). Leicestershire is NOT a Safety Valve authority and has no Delivering Better Value grant; the strategy is to hold 50% of the forecast deficit in the Budget Equalisation reserve. The S151 warns of a sector-wide S114 risk at override end.

GBP 85m of the four-year savings requirement is still unidentified; the MTFS gap rises to GBP 85m by 2029/30 (cumulative ~199m). The 2026/27 gap of GBP 18.1m is balanced by a draw from the Budget Equalisation reserve.
Children and Family Services and Adults and Communities carry GBP 36.9m of the GBP 48.4m four-year savings, the bulk, against rising LAC, UASC and adult social care demand.
